name: Coalition for Rainforest Nations (Founders Pledge, 2018)
summary: Diplomacy for rainforest countries in the UN climate talks, behind the REDD+ mechanism that pays countries to keep forests standing. A re-implementation of Founders Pledge's 2018 estimate of what CfRN's past work cost per tonne of CO₂e averted.

sections.title: Effect on national forestry plans (not in Founders Pledge's total)
From cost per tonne to tonnes per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' step after Founders Pledge's bottom line: Founders Pledge reports dollars per tonne; the site needs tonnes per dollar, and how much air pollution those tonnes cut. Forest carbon kept out of the air comes with no fossil-fuel smoke; only the smoke from fires used to clear forest counts, and it is small per tonne (docs/normalization.md 2.5). The tonnes come years after the money is spent, so they are discounted for that wait at the site's discount rate.

rows.label: Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge counts CfRN's spending from 2004 to 2017 (about 2010 on average) against REDD+ money pledged over 2006–14. REDD+ pays countries for forest kept after the fact, and Founders Pledge notes that only about $400 million had been paid out by 2015, so the forest the money keeps standing is mostly kept from the mid-2010s into the 2020s: about seven years after the average dollar, 3 to 12. Our judgment from Founders Pledge's dates. Founders Pledge counts a tonne the same whenever it is avoided; the site discounts every future benefit at the discount rate under Your values, in both views (an evaluator stating dollars per tonne takes no view on discounting). The heat deaths a tonne avoids are discounted again from the year it is avoided, in the site's climate conversion.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per dollar
rows.explainer: One over Founders Pledge's cost per tonne, discounted for the wait until the tonnes are avoided, like every future benefit on the site. How much air pollution these tonnes cut is the rows below.

rows.label: Air pollution per tonne of forest carbon kept, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne (fire smoke)

source.title: Reddington et al. (2015), Air quality and human health improvements from reductions in deforestation-related fire in Brazil, Nature Geoscience 8, 768–771; IPCC (2006), Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Vol. 4, Ch. 4 Forest Land
source.note: Reddington: deforestation in Brazil fell from 37,800 to 22,900 km² a year (2001–12), preventing about 400–1,700 premature adult deaths a year across South America. IPCC 2006 (https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/4_Volume4/V4_04_Ch4_Forest_Land.pdf): Table 4.7, tropical rain forest, North and South America, 300 (120–400) tonnes dry matter per ha above ground; Table 4.4, root-to-shoot ratio 0.37 for tropical rainforest; Table 4.3, carbon fraction 0.47.

rows.explainer: No fossil fuel is involved, but tropical forest is mostly cleared by fire, and its smoke kills. Reddington et al. (2015) find that Brazil's fall in deforestation, about 14,900 km² a year, prevents 400–1,700 deaths a year. IPCC's default for South American rain forest, 300 tonnes of dry matter a hectare above ground (120–400, Table 4.7), plus roots at 0.37 of that (Table 4.4), at 0.47 tonnes of carbon per tonne (Table 4.3), is about 190 tonnes of carbon or 710 tonnes of CO₂ a hectare, 71,000 a km²: about 1.05 billion tonnes a year. That is 0.4–1.6 deaths per million tonnes, 0.003–0.011 of the world-average fossil-fuel smoke per tonne (1.46 per 10,000); best guess 0.005, the middle on a log scale. Low 0, as Founders Pledge leaves fire smoke out and CfRN's tonnes also come from countries that clear forest with less fire; high 0.03, the top of Reddington's deaths with IPCC's lowest biomass.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: The row the site's climate conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): the air-pollution deaths each of these tonnes avoids, as a multiple of the world average behind the shared rate, 1.46 air-pollution deaths per 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ from fossil fuels (Rethink Priorities). The conversion values every tonne for its heat deaths (discounted over the decades until they come) and adds "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂"'s air-pollution part times this row, at once. Here it is the fire smoke above: none of these tonnes come from burning less fossil fuel.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The tonnes per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). The site turns these tonnes into years of healthy life through the deaths they avoid: "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂", its heat part discounted over "Years until the heat deaths from a tonne of CO₂" for every tonne, and its air-pollution part, at once, times "Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne" above.
